ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this case goes to a human reviewer and the disputed SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is placed on hold — neither collected from the rider nor refunded to her while review is pending. No money moves today.

What is established on the record. The driver did arrive and did wait. The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-08T09:30:20, and the GPS trace places the driver inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius from its first fix at 09:30:00, roughly 24 m from the PLQ pick-up pin, with 34 qualifying fixes, 100% coverage and no sampling gap. Measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, as POL-NS-01 limb (c) requires and not from the arrival tap, the driver held position in one continuous run of 330 seconds — 30 seconds more than the 300-second minimum for a LARGE_VENUE pickup — and terminated the trip at 09:35:30 on RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 are therefore met on this trip.

No rider-side clause displaces the fee. POL-NS-02's proximity test is satisfied on clean, accuracy-filtered evidence. POL-NS-05 is not engaged: at the arrival marker the driver was about 24 m from the pin and stationary at 0.0 kph, nowhere near the 300 m or 15 kph thresholds, so the marker is true. POL-NS-03 does not apply — every fix is inside the arrival radius and registered_pickup_points is 1, so neither the wrong-entrance nor the pin-ambiguity branch arises. POL-NS-06's strict-liability shortfall route gives the rider nothing: 330 seconds of effective dwell against a 300-second minimum (shortfall basis −30 seconds). POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider: limb (a) fails because the chat log holds no rider locating or coordinating message (only the SYSTEM 'Your driver has arrived' notice and the driver's own 'Waiting at PLQ 3 pickup bay.'), and limb (c) fails because the rider track places her device about 519 m from the pin, outside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius, with zero qualifying fixes. The rider advocate candidly does not press the waiting-period arithmetic, and I agree it gives the rider nothing.

Why no refund issues today. The reason is the driver's own trailing-30-day record, not the waiting arithmetic. POL-NS-07 withholds compensation where driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 4 or more AND that figure divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d exceeds 0.08. Both limbs are met on weight-1.0 profile evidence: 7 terminations, and 7 ÷ 70 = 0.10. Compensation is therefore withheld and POL-NS-09(d) compels escalation. For completeness, no rider-side escalation limb fires: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so POL-NS-09(c) and the rider limb of (d) are untriggered; and there is no POL-NS-09(b) direct contradiction on arrival, dwell or rider presence, since trip_record.arrived_at at 09:30:20 is 20 seconds from the nearest GPS fix, far inside the 90-second skew limit.

Two profile points, which each side correctly raised. The value 1 in rider_profile.prior_no_show_flags and the value 2 in driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags are lifetime counters and are CONTEXT ONLY under POL-GEN-01; they may not be substituted for the trailing-30-day counters that POL-NS-07 and POL-NS-09(d) actually read, and nothing in this ruling rests on them. And no adverse pattern finding attaches to the rider: the escalation is produced by the driver's pattern, and the citable rider counters are clean.

One artifact caveat, disclosed for completeness. EV-ADVIS-09108-01 (traffic advisory) is MISSING and carries weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it supplies no fact and POL-NS-06 limb (i) — which would allow separate in-geofence intervals to be summed — is unavailable to either side. It changes nothing here: the dwell is a single continuous 330-second run, no accumulation is required, and neither advocate relied on limb (i).

The escalation packet carries the instruction POL-NS-07 requires, recorded in the referrals list below. The fee is held meanwhile. The open question for the reviewer is whether this driver's 30-day no-show pattern is genuine fee-farming or an artefact of the trailing window; on that determination the SGD 4.00 is either refunded to the rider or released to the platform.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-07 (anti-farming branch): direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's SGD 4.00 cancellation fee in full; the fee is held, not collected or refunded, while review is pending.
